bc_upper_cat_wall.blurb: Upper Cat Wall is the larger of two cliffs above Arrow Lake, not far from Castlegar in the West Kootenay. Sixteen routes share it, mostly bolted lines plus a handful protected by gear. A few easier leads from 5.6 to 5.9 exist, but the bulk sits between 5.10 and 5.12, with one harder outlier. Expect steep, exposed climbing on faces, cracks and a few roofs, with pitches of roughly 18 to 30 m. Some of the newer lines still shed loose rock, so a helmet is a good idea. The wall is only a few minutes above its smaller neighbour, and it has a name as a spring destination.
bc_upper_cat_wall.parking_note: Leave the car at the lakeside pullout with a red gate, about 1 km past the dam when driving in from Castlegar or Nelson on the road toward Robson.
bc_upper_cat_wall.approach: Cross the road from the pullout and follow the cairned, cut trail through the forest to Lower Cat Wall. Bear right at the fork and zigzag up the slope; the upper wall comes about three minutes past the lower cliff.

bc_off_white.blurb: Off White is a quiet, somewhat overlooked crag in the White Walls cluster at Skaha Bluffs, above Skaha Lake near Penticton. Its sixteen lines are almost all bolted, with a single gear route, and stand about 20 to 25 m tall. Grades lean toward the middle and upper end: a lone easier line, a few in the 5.10s, and the majority in the 5.11 and low 5.12 range. The original routes have been re-equipped with stainless hardware and several new lines were added, so it makes a pleasant change from the busier walls nearby.

bc_fairytale.blurb: Fairytale is a bouldering spot in the Syringa area of the West Kootenay, set in open, old-burn forest and field close to Arrow Lake. Sixteen problems are recorded, spanning an easy V1 up to V8, with a good cluster of V4 to V7 lines and only a few at the lower end. The standout feature is a big cave and overhang that gives steep, powerful climbing, and the zone has a reputation as a real gem with plenty of variety. It lies a short drive and walk from the other Syringa boulders, so it pairs easily with them for a full day.

bc_croissant_wall.blurb: Croissant Wall is a sport crag on Cedar Mountain above Kelowna, inside a regional park in the Okanagan. All sixteen routes are bolted, mostly 20 to 25 m with a few longer, and the grade spread is skewed hard: a single 5.8, a few 5.10s, and the majority in the 5.11 and low 5.12 range. The wall is steep in places and vertical elsewhere, with positive holds and pumpy finishes. It faces south, so it catches sun through the day and is considered a good spring choice. The rock has a bubbly, flaky look that gave the wall its name.

bc_the_courtyard.blurb: The Courtyard is a recently developed sport crag in the forest off the Mamquam road, north of the Chief at Squamish. Of sixteen routes, fifteen are bolted and one is a top-rope line. Routes are 12 to 18 m and cover a wide range, from a 5.5 beginner line through a solid middle in the 5.8 to 5.11 range, up to a 5.12a. The wall mixes a clean face with crimps and some overhanging sections. It dries quickly and picks up plenty of sun. Wear a helmet since the crag is still new, and avoid top-rope setups from above.
bc_the_courtyard.parking_note: Drive east along the Mamquam road from Highway 99, then turn onto Powerhouse Springs road; the crag is a short way down it, close to a large roadside boulder.

bc_parkland.blurb: Parkland is a newer forest sport crag just off the Powerhouse Springs road near Squamish, with sixteen bolted routes put up in 2016 and 2017. The grades cluster tightly: ten routes sit in the 5.10 range, a couple at 5.9, a few at 5.11 and a single 5.12 line, which makes it a good stop for steady climbers working through the low-to-mid grades. A 60 m rope is wise for everything, and a helmet is recommended. Do not scramble above to rig top ropes, as loose debris can drop onto the people below.

bc_lakeside_wall.blurb: Lakeside Wall is the hard-climbing wall at Ellison Park, right beside the water near Vernon. It faces west, so mornings are shaded and the afternoon brings sun. Most of its sixteen routes are bolted, and they are punchy and sustained: the core of the grades is 5.12 and 5.13, with a few easier leads and two V4 traverses for variety. The granite is solid and the setting by the lake is a bonus. Easier trad and top-rope climbing is on the park's Main Wall nearby, so mixed groups can split up.
